title: Show a preview that stops where the entitlement begins
statement: An unentitled request receives a self-contained excerpt describing what the full item covers, and the withheld remainder is absent from the response body rather than present and hidden by styling.
rationale: Content removed only by styling is still delivered, so a paywall implemented that way publishes the item to anyone who reads the response while showing a wall to the reader who paid for it.
implementation: Decide the excerpt on the server from the entitlement result and emit only that, so no branch of the template can serialise the withheld remainder into an unentitled response.

verification.method: Request paywalled routes without credentials and search the raw response body for text that appears only in the entitled rendering.

caution: The cited documentation describes how to mark a section as paywalled, not how much of an item to give away, so the length of the excerpt is a commercial decision this process reports on rather than sets.

title: Declare paywalled sections with the documented access markup
statement: A page serving a restricted excerpt says so in its structured description, naming the sections that are withheld by a selector that matches the rendered markup.
rationale: Without the declaration a truncated excerpt is indistinguishable from a page that is simply thin, and a selector that no longer matches the markup declares a boundary that is not there.
implementation: Emit the selector from the same constant the template uses for the withheld region, so renaming the region cannot leave the declaration pointing at a class that no longer exists.

verification.method: Parse the access declaration from each paywalled route and confirm every declared selector matches at least one element in the served markup.

title: Serve one canonical address whether or not the reader is entitled
statement: The entitled and unentitled renderings of an item share a single address and declare the same canonical value, with no separate preview address and no query parameter recording access state.
rationale: Splitting the two renderings across addresses creates a duplicate pair whose members differ only in what the reader may see, and the address that accumulates links is then the one nobody can read in full.
implementation: Branch on entitlement inside the handler for the single address rather than redirecting to a preview route, and carry access state in the session rather than in the address.

verification.method: Request each paywalled item with and without credentials and compare the final address, status, and canonical value returned by both.

title: Serve crawlers the preview rather than the entitled body
statement: An automated client receives the same restricted excerpt an unentitled reader receives, and entitlement is never granted on the basis of a user-agent string or a source address.
rationale: Granting access by declared identity both publishes the item to anyone who copies that identity and shows search clients a page no reader can reach, which is the substitution the platform policy prohibits.
implementation: Resolve entitlement only from the credential the request presents, and let the access markup rather than an identity exemption tell search clients why the response is short.

verification.method: Request paywalled routes with a search-crawler user-agent and with an ordinary one, both unentitled, and compare the two response bodies for divergence.

caution: This is the one documented case where a restricted excerpt may differ from what an entitled reader sees, and it is narrower than it looks: the excerpt served to a crawler must match the excerpt served to an unentitled reader, not the entitled body.

sources.title: Spam policies for Google web search

title: Keep the metering counter out of the address
statement: A metered allowance is tracked in the session or the account rather than in the address, so no counter value appears as a path segment or a query parameter on a public item.
rationale: A counter in the address turns one item into an address per allowance state, and each of those addresses is fetchable and linkable while describing the same item.
implementation: Hold the allowance server-side against the session or account identifier and let the address stay constant as the allowance is consumed.

verification.method: Consume a metered allowance across successive requests and confirm the address of the item is unchanged at each step.

caution: Whether metered access is offered at all is a commercial decision. This record governs only where the counter is stored once metering exists.

title: Mark every withheld section where an item is split
statement: An item whose restricted portion is spread across several regions declares each of those regions, rather than declaring the first and leaving the rest undeclared.
rationale: A partial declaration describes the page as less restricted than it is, so the undeclared regions read as content the page simply lacks rather than content it is withholding.
implementation: Collect the withheld regions as a list during rendering and emit the declaration from that list, so an item with three restricted regions declares three rather than one.

verification.method: Count withheld regions in the served markup of multi-part items and compare that count against the number of regions the access declaration names.
